summary: The boundary-proof successor gate passed at the round-two head. Leg 1 closes the initialization-ordering gap: the new probe never calls EnvUtils or the timeout helper before startup, and the JVM class-init log proves EnvUtils initializes inside NodeConfig.loadNodeConfig in every case, with both legacy spellings and both precedence orders producing the expected waits at the real startup client. Leg 2 closes the session-timeout gap: instead of inferring the timeout from elapsed time, the probe captured the startup client's actual ConnectRequest at a local accepting peer; its session-timeout field reads exactly 30001 ms in the fallback case and 2000 ms with the explicit override, and it is the only field that differs between the two packets. One host fact was established on the way: bare JVMs on this Linux host need -Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=true for loopback, because without it JVM loopback connects are hairpinned through the sandbox fabric and never reach a local listener; all probe JVMs ran with the flag, as every Gradle JVM here already does. The round-two receipt's other results stand untouched; nothing was rerun, and no branch or PR content changed.
